source_refs.note: Exercise 11.3, Question 3: light-house 100 m, angles of depression 17 and 19 degrees; distance between the ships. Answer key PDF 309 (printed 36.78 m corrected).

blocks.prompt: 3 A man on the top of a 100 m high light-house is in line with two ships on the same side of it, whose angles of depression from the man are \(17^{\circ}\) and \(19^{\circ}\) respectively. Find the distance between the ships.
blocks.explanation:
A heights-and-distances question with angles of depression.
We need the gap between the two ships.
Plan: find each ship's distance from the foot with \(\cot\), then subtract.
steps:
Given: height \(AB = 100\) m; angles of depression \(17^{\circ}\) (far ship C) and \(19^{\circ}\) (near ship D); both ships on the same side.
To find: \(CD\).
Method: The angle of depression from A equals the angle of elevation from the ship (alternate angles). In each right triangle, \(\text{base} = \text{height} \times \cot(\text{angle})\).

Draw the figure
Why: The smaller angle (\(17^{\circ}\)) belongs to the farther ship C: looking at something far away you look down less steeply. So \(BC > BD\) and \(CD = BC - BD\).

Distance of the far ship
\[\tan 17^{\circ} = \dfrac{AB}{BC}\]
\[BC = 100\cot 17^{\circ}\]
\[= 100 \times 3.2709 = 327.09 \text{ m}\]
Why: In right triangle ABC, the angle at C is \(17^{\circ}\) (alternate to the depression angle); \(\tan = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}\).

Distance of the near ship
\[BD = 100\cot 19^{\circ}\]
\[= 100 \times 2.9042 = 290.42 \text{ m}\]
Why: Same method in triangle ABD with angle \(19^{\circ}\) at D.

Subtract
\[CD = BC - BD\]
\[= 100(\cot 17^{\circ} - \cot 19^{\circ})\]
\[\approx 327.09 - 290.42\]
\[\approx 36.66 \text{ m}\]
Why: Both ships are on the same side, on one line with B, so the gap is the difference. (Without rounding the cotangents first: \(36.664\ldots\) m.)

Check
\[\tan^{-1}\!\left(\tfrac{100}{327.09}\right) \approx 17.0^{\circ} \;\checkmark\]
\[\tan^{-1}\!\left(\tfrac{100}{290.42}\right) \approx 19.0^{\circ} \;\checkmark\]
Why: The two distances give back the two given angles.
blocks.final_answer: Distance between the ships \(\approx 36.66\) m (about 36.7 m)

answer_figure.alt: To-scale drawing: a 100 m light-house AB stands at the right with the man at its top A. A dashed horizontal line goes left from A. Two lines of sight go down to the ships: to D at 19 degrees below the horizontal and to C, farther left, at 17 degrees. BD is about 290.42 m and the gap CD is about 36.66 m.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints distance \(= 36.78\) m. This is wrong: \(100(\cot 17^{\circ} - \cot 19^{\circ}) = 100(3.27085 - 2.90421) = 36.66\) m (36.67 m with four-figure tables). The correct distance is about 36.66 m.
